(a) superluminal motion in compact radio sources is frequently complex; (b) the superluminal motion seen is consistent with the emission being produced by shocks; (c) there is evidence for a change in the physical conditions in parsec-scale jet beyond which other factors, e.g., plasma interactions, may be important; (d) multifrequency and polarization imaging are emerging as critical tests of model predictions.

the parsec-scale structure in these sources is complex, and that the underlying jet flow can be highly dynamic and variable, as evidenced by the complex kinematics and the presence of stationary features.
